title: Row-Level Security (RLS) for Multi-Tenant Database Architecture
realWorldScenario: A multi-tenant SaaS application shares a single PostgreSQL database across 1,200 enterprise tenants. An engineer accidentally forgets `WHERE tenant_id = ?` in a new microservice endpoint, exposing Tenant A’s data to Tenant B.
questionStatement: Design an end-to-end Row-Level Security (RLS) policy in PostgreSQL that guarantees tenant isolation at the database engine level. Explain `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, setting session context via `current_setting()`, and why `SUPERUSER` or `BYPASSRLS` roles can bypass tenant isolation.
expectedConcepts: ALTER TABLE ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY to restrict table owners
USING (for read/delete) vs WITH CHECK (for insert/update)
SET LOCAL transaction scoping in pooled connections
hints: What happens if the table owner executes a query without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY?
How does SET LOCAL ensure tenant ID does not leak to the next client using the pooled connection?
Difference between USING (filtering existing rows) and WITH CHECK (validating inserted/updated rows).
